feedback.message:
REPAIR REQUEST: Snake Game — Key handling defect + pause resume on button

Finding 1 (confirmed): The "P" key handler does NOT call e.preventDefault().

In the keydown event handler at line ~367, the "p" case toggles pause but falls through to the default branch. Unlike the spacebar (line 363) and arrow keys (line 372), 'p' does not get preventDefault() called. This means pressing P may trigger browser default behavior (page scroll, find-in-page, or other platform-specific shortcuts). The fix is to add e.preventDefault() before toggling pause in the "p" case, same as the spacebar already does.

Finding 2 (behavioral concern): The "R" key restart has no guard condition.

Pressing R calls start() unconditionally even while a game is actively running (score > 0, not yet game-over). If you press R mid-game by accident, the score resets to 0 with no warning. Consider either:
- Adding a guard like "if (!running || gameOver) { start(); }" so restart only works when the game isn't running, OR
- Keeping the current behavior but this is expected design — in that case no fix needed, just note it.

The original brief says "restart" should be present; R providing an immediate restart mid-game is actually a valid feature, not necessarily a bug. I flag it only because accidental mid-game resets could frustrate players. If the intent is to allow mid-game restart, this is fine as-is.

Priority: Fix Finding 1 (P key missing preventDefault). This is a real behavioral defect that will be observable in any browser.
feedback.reason: Confirmed defect: P key handler missing preventDefault; may trigger browser default behavior. Also flagged R-key unrestricted restart as behavioral concern.
